6 Maintenance Tips for Asphalt Shingle Roofs in Allentown

3 July 2025 Roof Maintenance

Your roof protects everything beneath it, your family, your belongings, and your home’s value. In Allentown, Pennsylvania, where heavy snow, summer sun, and sudden storms can wreak havoc on roofing materials, following these maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is essential to preserving your investment.

Whether you’re a longtime resident or new to the Lehigh Valley, these six tips will help extend the life of your shingles and save you money on repairs or replacements down the line.

Inspect Your Roof Twice a Year

The first and most important of all maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is a biannual inspection. Check in early spring and late fall, or after any major storm.

During an inspection, look for:

  • Missing or curling shingles
  • Granule loss (check gutters for debris)
  • Exposed nail heads
  • Algae or moss growth

In Allentown’s mixed climate, from snow-packed winters to stormy springs, shingles wear faster than in mild regions. Hiring a local roofer for a yearly checkup is a smart move if you’re unsure what to look for.

Keep Your Gutters Clear Year-Round

Clogged gutters are a hidden threat to your roof. Water that can’t drain properly backs up under shingles and damages roof decking. One of the most underrated maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is to keep gutters and downspouts clean.

In Allentown, where leafy neighborhoods like West End and Old Fairgrounds are common, fall cleanup is especially critical. Gutter guards can also help reduce buildup and keep drainage flowing smoothly throughout the year.

Trim Back Overhanging Tree Branches

Overhanging branches is a danger to your roof. They:

  • Scratch and tear shingles
  • Drop debris that holds moisture
  • Attract animals that may nest in your attic

One of the top maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is to trim any tree limbs that reach within 5–10 feet of your roofline. This is particularly important in storm-prone areas like Allentown, where strong winds can turn branches into projectiles.

Check Flashing and Seals Around Roof Penetrations

Shingles aren’t the only parts of your roof that need attention. Flashing around chimneys, vents, skylights, and dormers can loosen over time. Damaged flashing leads to one of the most common leak sources in asphalt shingle roofs.

As part of your seasonal maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs, check that all seals are tight, flashing is rust-free, and caulking hasn’t cracked.

Address Algae and Moss Early

Allentown’s humid summers can create perfect conditions for moss and algae to grow on north-facing or shaded roofs. While it might look harmless, it traps moisture and degrades your shingles.

One of the smart maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is to:

  • Install zinc or copper strips at the ridge
  • Wash your roof gently with a 50/50 mix of water and bleach
  • Avoid pressure washing, it can remove granules and void your warranty

Acting early prevents roof rot and costly damage later.

Schedule a Professional Roof Maintenance Service

No list of maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs is complete without recommending professional service. Even if you’re handy with a ladder, a trained roofer will spot issues you might miss.

Bonus Tips for Roof Longevity

Here are a few extra maintenance tips for asphalt shingle roofs that go a long way:

  • Install attic ventilation to reduce heat buildup
  • Apply algae-resistant shingle treatments every 2–3 years
  • Document your roof’s condition annually with photos for warranty purposes

The more proactive you are, the longer your roof will last.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long should an asphalt shingle roof last in Allentown?

With proper maintenance, 20–30 years or longer.

Can I walk on my roof to inspect it?

Only if it’s safe and stable. Otherwise, hire a pro to avoid damage or injury.

Is moss really that bad for shingles?

Yes. Moss retains moisture, causing shingle lift, decay, and leaks.

How do I know if my shingles are failing?

Look for bald spots, curling edges, or excessive granules in gutters.

Does insurance cover roof maintenance?

Typically no. But it often covers damage if caused by storms, provided you’ve done your part with regular care.
